kp8:0.2: The Discourse on the Amount of Savings
kp8:1.1: A man stores his savings in a deep pit close to water (thinking):
kp8:1.3: “When a duty or need has arisen it will be there to help me,
kp8:2.1: o to free me from a king if slandered, or from molestation
kp8:2.4: from a thief, or from a debt, or famine, or accident.”
kp8:2.5: For this kind of help, savings are stored up in the world.
kp8:3.2: Although it is well stored in a deep pit, close to water,
kp8:3.4: still, it cannot help him in all things on every occasion,
kp8:4.2: for perhaps those savings are removed from that place, or he forgets the signs (telling where they lie),
kp8:4.4: or nāgas take them away, or yakkhas carry them off,
kp8:5.2: or the heirs he dislikes extract them unseen,
kp8:5.3: and when his merit comes to an end all of it will be destroyed.
kp8:6.1: o But that woman or man who through giving, virtue,
kp8:6.4: restraint, and self-control has well stored up his savings,
kp8:7.2: (placing them) in a shrine, or in the Sangha, or in an individual, or a guest,
kp8:7.4: or in his mother or father, also in an elder brother,
kp8:8.1: those savings are well stored up, they follow one, they do not decay.
kp8:8.4: (Riches) he gives up when he has to leave (this life) but this goes along (with him).
kp8:9.1: It is not shared with others, no thief carries those savings away,
kp8:9.3: the wise man should make merit, (for) those savings follow one along.
kp8:10.2: These savings satisfy every desire of gods and men,
kp8:10.3: whatever they wish for, through this (merit) they receive all.
kp8:11.1: A good appearance, a good voice, a good shape, a good form,
kp8:11.4: sovereignty, and a retinue, through this (merit) they receive all.
kp8:12.1: A local kingship, an empire, and whatever happiness a Wheel-Rolling (King) has,
kp8:12.3: also godly kingship in the heavens, through this (merit) they receive all.
kp8:13.1: Human good fortune, delight in the world of the gods,
kp8:13.3: even the attainment of Emancipation, through this (merit) they receive all.
kp8:14.1: With the attainment of (good) friends, devotion to systematic (thought),
kp8:14.3: there is the power of understanding and freedom, through this (merit) they receive all.
kp8:15.1: The discriminations, and the liberations, and whatever perfections the disciples have,
kp8:15.3: Independent Awakening, the Buddhas’ ground, through this (merit) they receive all.
kp8:16.2: So this is of great benefit, that is to say, the attainment of merit,
kp8:16.3: therefore the wise and intelligent (always) praise the making of merit.
